related_prs.title: 5100001: exact four-period counterexample to printed k107
related_prs.body:
## Exact counterexample to the printed k107 product

Refutes the literal invariant in both arXiv v11 Table 2 and the published journal Table 2. In the ellipse with axes 4 and 3, two primitive convex four-period billiard orbits share the confocal caustic with axes 16/5 and 9/5, but give k107 values 288/625 and 625/1152.

The proof checks the source's original-orbit half angles and outer tangent polygon, provides a continuous T²=−id family connecting the examples, and verifies common caustic, physical reflection and all nonzero denominators. Signed and ordinary areas coincide because both examples are convex and counterclockwise.

Separate adversarial AI review passed without correction. The frozen proof is unchanged. All 10,073 submitted exact controls replay byte-identically; 8,397 independent rational/symbolic controls pass. Eight review files are included.

Two substantive approach families are recorded (2/5). This resolves the printed assertion by counterexample. It does not claim a corrected quotient/parity theorem, historical priority, or human peer review. The related k108 and earlier k603/k405 targets are distinct. related_prs.title: Disprove the printed elliptic-billiard k108 quotient by exact six-period orbits
related_prs.body:
## Exact counterexample to the printed k108 assertion

Two convex primitive six-period orbits in the ellipse x²/4+y²=1 share the same nondegenerate confocal caustic lambda=4/9 and perimeter 28/3. Their outer-area ratio divided by the product of internal half-angle sines equals 11664/3125 and 3645/1024, respectively. The exact positive difference disproves the source assertion for N≡2(mod4).

Both arXiv v11 Table 2 and published Table 2 visibly give this quotient and parity. The package checks actual tangent contacts, ordinary reflection, distinct vertices, all outer tangent intersections, signed areas and half-angle values. All 291 exact controls pass; no floating-point simulation is used.

The construction and related campaign geometry are credited. Historical priority is unconfirmed; no corrected all-period theorem, official erratum or human peer-review claim is made. Separate adversarial AI review passed without mandatory corrections: all 291 author assertions replayed byte-identically and 272 independent exact rational controls passed. The complete eight-file review bundle is included. One approach; parent owns the queue update.

related_prs.title: 5100010: identify k120 as a reviewed bicentric-theorem consequence
related_prs.body:
## Source-status result

**Already solved by a published-theorem consequence; one reduction approach logged.** The focal-angle invariant k120 follows from Roitman–Garcia–Reznik’s 2021 bicentric cosine-sum theorem. This package provides a complete source audit and explicit coordinate/ordinary-angle bridge: focal polarity sends the fixed nested confocal ellipse pair to nested circles, and each original focal cosine is minus the internal-angle cosine of the polar polygon.

The scope includes simple and star Poncelet orbits in the original nondegenerate confocal-ellipse setting, with no parity restriction. The independent review explicitly checks the published Jacobi step/winding convention by a doubled traversal. This is credited existing mathematics, with no new-discovery claim or unsupported hyperbolic-caustic extension.
